questions.q:
A series is given with one term missing. Select the correct alternative from the given ones that will complete the series.

500, 494, 486, 476, ?, 450, 434, 416
questions.solution:
Subtract successive even numbers: 6,8,10,12,14,16,18. The missing term is 476−12=464.

**Answer: 464**

questions.q:
Select the option that is related to the fifth letter cluster in the same way as the second letter cluster is related to the first letter cluster and fourth letter cluster is related to third letter cluster.

ZNV : WKS :: QIP : NFM :: TEY : ?
questions.solution:
Move each letter back three places. TEY becomes QBV.

**Answer: QBV**

questions.q:
A series is given with one term missing. Select the correct alternative from the given ones that will complete the series.

VT, SO, PJ, ME, ?, GU, DP, AK
questions.solution:
The first letter decreases by 3 and the second by 5, wrapping after A. ME becomes JZ.

**Answer: JZ**

questions.q:
In the following question, set of letter clusters are given. The letter clusters of each set are related to the letter clusters of the same set by some Logic/Rule/Relation. From the given alternatives, select a group of letter clusters which follows the same Logic/Rule/Relation.

(FA, BV, XQ)

(HL, DG, ZB)
questions.solution:
Each transition shifts the first letter back 4 and the second back 5. GY→CT→YO follows the rule.

**Answer: (GY, CT, YO)**

questions.q: January 5 of a leap year is Wednesday. How many total Saturdays and Thursdays are there in February of that year?
questions.solution:
The given weekday makes January 1 a Saturday and February 1 a Tuesday. A 29-day February then has four Thursdays and four Saturdays, totaling eight.

**Answer: 8**

questions.q:
In the year 1924, which of the following month had 5 Thursdays?

I. March

II. May
questions.solution:
Calendar calculation gives four Thursdays in March 1924 and five in May 1924. Thus only II is correct.

**Answer: Only II**

questions.q: 5 persons C, D, F, G and H are sitting in a row facing north (not necessarily in the same order). Only C and F are to the left of D. Only H is to the right of G. F is at one of the extreme ends of the row. How many persons are sitting between F and G?
questions.solution:
The row is F,C,D,G,H. The persons between F and G are C and D, so there are two.

**Answer: 2**

questions.q:
Height of 6 girls P, Q, R, S, T and U is compared. Height of no two girls is same. R is taller than only four girls. U is taller than both S and P. S and P both are taller than both Q and T. Which of the following is a possible sequence of their heights?

I. U > R > S > P > T > Q 

II. U > R > P > S > Q > T
questions.solution:
Both sequences put R second-tallest, U above S and P, and S/P above Q/T. Neither condition fixes the relative order within those lower pairs.

**Answer: Both I and II**

questions.q:
Select the option that is related to the second letter-number cluster in the same way as the third letter-number cluster is related to the fourth letter-number cluster and fifth letter-number cluster is related to sixth letter-number cluster.

(NOTE: Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the numbers into its constituent digits. E.g.13 – Operations on 13 such as adding /subtracting /multiplying etc. to 13 can be performed. Breaking down 13 into 1 and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1 and 3 is not allowed)

? : AV60 :: SK18 : TM36 :: BN25 : CP50
questions.solution:
The transformation shifts letters forward 1 and 2, then doubles the number. Reverse it on AV60 to get ZT30.

**Answer: ZT30**

questions.q:

(NOTE: Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the numbers into its constituent digits. BI320 : GB450 :: DJ110 : ? :: EK240 : JD370

questions.q:
Select the option that is related to the third number in the same way as the second number is related to the first number and sixth number is related to fifth number.

(NOTE: Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the numbers into its constituent digits. E.g.13 – Operations on 13 such as adding /subtracting /multiplying etc. to 13 can be performed. Breaking down 13 into 1 and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1 and 3 is not allowed)

 9165 : 9123 :: 5630 : ? :: 874 : 832
questions.solution:
Subtract 42 from the first number. Thus 5630−42=5588.

questions.q:

(NOTE: Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the numbers into its constituent digits. In a certain coded language 'JAMB' is coded as 'KBNC' and 'BOND' is coded as 'CPOE'. How will 'COIR' be coded in the same code language?
questions.solution:
Move every letter forward one alphabet place. COIR becomes DPJS.

questions.q:
A series is given with one term wrong. Select that wrong term from the given alternatives.

WP14, XT28, YX42, ZB56, AF70, BK84
questions.solution:
The first letter advances by 1 and the second by 4, with numbers increasing by 14. After AF70 should come BJ84, so BK84 is wrong.

**Answer: BK84**

questions.q:

FAN1000, AVI907, ?, QLY721, LGT628
questions.solution:
Move all letters back five places and subtract 93 from the number. AVI907 is followed by VQD814.

**Answer: VQD814**

questions.q: In 24 hours, how many × minute and hour hands of a clock overlap?
questions.solution:
The hands overlap eleven times in twelve hours. Therefore they overlap twenty-two times in twenty-four hours.

**Answer: 22**

questions.q: Angle between minute hand and hour hand of a clock at 3:05 and 11:55 are J and K respectively. What is the difference (in degrees) between J and K ?
questions.solution:
At 3:05, the hand angles are 92.5° and 30°, a gap of 62.5°. At 11:55 they are 357.5° and 330°, a gap of 27.5°. Difference=35°.

**Answer: 35**

questions.q: The sum of present ages of S and T is 50 years. The difference of the present ages of S and T is 8 years. 6 years ago from present, what was the ratio of age of S to age of T? (S is elder to T)
questions.solution:
Present ages are (50+8)/2=29 and (50−8)/2=21. Six years earlier they were 23 and 15, giving 23:15.

**Answer: 23 : 15**
